Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Deepak Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Shatrughna Yadav, learned
Aga for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
316 of 2023, under Sections 498-A, 376, 377, 323, 506 IPC & 3/4 D.P. Act & 3/4 Muslim Women (Protection of Rights of Marriage) Act and 3/5(1) U.P. Prohibition of Unlawful Conversion of religion Act, Police Station- Majhola, District- Moradabad, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

sentences.text:
3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 28.04.2023 against the applicant and according to the FIR,
applicant by playing fraud performed marriage with the informant and he did not disclose that he is Muslim and after marriage, he continuously sexually exploited the informant and also committed unnatural sexual offence.

Jamal Khan @ Sonu vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7952501/
1 4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 24.04.2023 applicant gave her triple talaq and he had already performed marriage about 18 years before with one Farah and also having two children from her and also continuously harassing the informant for dowry.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and admittedly applicant is the husband of the informant and therefore,
there is no question for offence under Section 376 IPC.

He further submitted that actually applicant and informant belong to different communities and this fact was well known to the informant and after knowing that applicant is Muslim, she performed marriage with the applicant and from the wedlock of the applicant and informant a child was also born and this fact has been admitted by the informant in the FIR.

6. He further submitted that unfortunately after marriage some dispute arose between husband and wife and in this regard on 01.04.2023 a compromise was executed between them, which has been annexed as Annexure No. 4 to the affidavit and according to compromise, due to dispute arose between them, they are free to live independently and they will not having any concern with each other but in spite of that after about three weeks, informant lodged FIR of the present case totally on the basis of false and frivolous allegations.
7.

He further submitted that if informant is being tortured and harassed by the applicant i.e. her husband then only offence under Section 498-A IPC can be made out and for maintenance,
informant can file an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 30.04.2023.

8. Per contra, learned AGA although, opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the fact that as per Annexure No. 4 to the affidavit, on 01.04.2023 a compromise was executed between applicant and informant of the case and thereafter FIR of the present case was lodged after about more than 27 days.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. Admittedly, applicant is the husband of the informant and it appears that, both belong to different communities and after marriage, some dispute arose between husband and wife and on 01.04.2023 they decided to live separately and in this regard a compromise was also executed between them (Annexure No. 4) but after about 27 days, FIR of the present case was lodged by the informant i.e. wife of the applicant.
11. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
12. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant- Jamal Khan @ Sonu be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
14. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

15. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 21.7.2023 KK Patel  Jamal Khan @ Sonu vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7952501/
